title: Fix routing snapshot staleness that triggered cascading model handoffs and cross-region loop
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed a multi-region incident where requests were silently swapped to incompatible model variants and several regions entered a short-lived reroute loop. The immediate customer impact was elevated latency and an increase in API errors for customers pinned to certain model versions. This ticket captures the root-cause analysis, mitigations already applied, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.

What happened (brief): A delayed snapshot propagation combined with an optimistic local routing decision allowed a routing node to serve requests with an incompatible model variant. That node triggered retries and fanout which, due to stale snapshot TTLs and a lack of a compatibility guard, amplified into a cross-region reroute loop for ~12 minutes before the automated capacity breaker engaged.

Detection: Alerts: routing-error-rate spike (SLO alert), regional latency SLO breaches. First pager at 2026-03-09T14:07Z. Root-cause triage completed 2026-03-09T18:20Z.

Root cause hypothesis: 1) Snapshot propagation lag from policy control plane to edge routing cache under a transient write lock; 2) Router decision engine allowed local cached policy to win without validating model binary compatibility; 3) Fallback policy defaulted to a generic variant that lacked architecture match, producing silent incompatibility errors; 4) Retry/backoff logic lacked circuit constraints at the region boundary which allowed oscillation.

Impact: Approximately 2.4% of hosted API calls during the window experienced higher error rates and increased tail latency. Affected customers included both Hosted API and some Dedicated tenants that used sticky routing rules.

Mitigation applied during incident: - Forced policy snapshot eviction across the affected routing shard (mitigation script run 2026-03-09T14:20Z). - Temporarily widened circuit-breaker thresholds to prevent customer-visible throttles while engineers stabilized routing state. - Emergency rollback of a recent policy-serving optimization that reduced propagation ACKs.

Accepted resolution criteria: 1) No silent model-compatibility swaps in canary runs across two full business days. 2) New compatibility guard reduces incompatible-serving errors to zero in e2e tests. 3) Telemetry surfaced within 5 minutes for any routing-state divergence > 30s.

Action items (owner — due):
- Implement epoch-based snapshot versioning with monotonic sequence numbers and server-side validation so routers refuse to serve if local epoch is older than control-plane epoch by > 2. (Diego Romero — due 2026-03-18)
- Add a pre-serve model-compatibility check in the router: verify model architecture/quantization fingerprint matches the requested variant and return deterministic fallback to last-known-compatible variant rather than generic default. (Lina Huang — due 2026-03-21)
action_items: [A1] Epoched snapshots: add monotonic epoch and enforced reject-on-stale (>2) behavior at router (owner: Diego Romero, estimate: 3) — due 2026-03-18
[A2] Compatibility guard: router validates model binary fingerprint before serving and aborts silent swaps (owner: Lina Huang, estimate: 5) — due 2026-03-21
[A3] Fallback policy change: change default fallback to 'reject-and-failover-to-control-plane' rather than 'generic-variant' for mismatches (owner: Product/Runtime, estimate: 2) — due 2026-03-24

[A4] Regional circuit constraints: implement region-bound circuit breaker preventing fanout beyond 3 remote regions per minute for a single request origin (owner: Marco Silva, estimate: 3) — due 2026-03-19
[A5] Snapshot telemetry: dashboard and alert for snapshot-propagation-lag > 15s per shard (owner: Observability team, estimate: 2) — due 2026-03-15
[A6] Automated canary: run cross-region canaries that exercise variant swaps under controlled load for 48h post-rollout (owner: SRE, estimate: 4) — due 2026-03-28
[A7] Runbook and playbook: create a runbook for 'routing-state divergence' including quick eviction, regional throttle knobs, and rollback steps (owner: Oncall lead, estimate: 2) — due 2026-03-16
[A8] Testing: add unit+integration tests that simulate delayed snapshot propagation and assert no incompatible-serving occurs (owner: QA, estimate: 3) — due 2026-03-22
[A9] Postmortem review: schedule cross-team retro and share learnings with Product and Support (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate: 1) — due 2026-03-12
action_status_summary: Initial mitigations completed; A9 retro held 2026-03-11. A5 (telemetry) in progress; A1 started (PR opened). A2 is design-complete and awaiting implementation slot. A4 design reviewed. Remaining items scheduled against routing-2026.04 sprint.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Observability team: Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/snapshot-propagation. Alert rule added to staging.

postmortem_notes: Primary gap: router too permissive when serving from local cache in the presence of snapshot-propagation delays. Secondary gap: fallback policy favored availability over compatibility and amplified silent failures. Recommend treating compatibility as a first-class safety check in the serving path. We also recommend refactoring snapshot propagation to be more transactional and introducing simpler invariants (epoch monotonicity + canary rollouts).
next_steps: Finish PRs for epoched snapshots and compatibility guard, run the 48h canary, validate metrics, and then roll into routing-2026.04. After rollout, run a targeted audit of other fallback codepaths that may default to incompatible variants.
